The variable is described in the problem as the temperature difference between top and bottom surfaces. The cited record (pq_temperature_difference) defines a temperature difference with SI dimension Theta (dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,1,0,0]), directly supporting the candidate Theta exponent of +1 and the absence of other base dimensions.

The ledger entry labels lambda as the thermal conductivity in the heat-transfer context. The cited record (pq_thermal_conductivity) explicitly gives thermal conductivity with SI dimension M L T^-3 Theta^-1 (dimension_vector [1,1,-3,0,-1,0,0]), which matches the candidate exponents for lambda.

The problem uses g for gravitational acceleration. The cited record (pq_gravitational_acceleration) defines g as acceleration with SI dimension L T^-2 (dimension_vector [0,1,-2,0,0,0,0]), which matches the candidate exponents for g.

The problem statement designates alpha as the thermal expansion coefficient. The cited record (pq_thermal_expansion_coefficient) defines this coefficient as having SI dimension Theta^-1 (dimension_vector [0,0,0,0,-1,0,0]); this directly supports the candidate exponent Theta = -1 and zeros for the other base dimensions.

The ledger names nu as kinematic viscosity. The cited record (pq_kinematic_viscosity) provides kinematic viscosity with SI dimension L^2 T^-1 (dimension_vector [0,2,-1,0,0,0,0]), matching the candidate exponents for nu.

The problem uses kappa for thermal diffusivity. The cited record (pq_thermal_diffusivity) explicitly lists thermal diffusivity with SI dimension L^2 T^-1 (dimension_vector [0,2,-1,0,0,0,0]), which supports the candidate exponents for kappa.
